request.searchQuestion: Which primary research papers establish accurate and reproducible parallel floating-point summation for scientific simulations, and what performance and numerical reproducibility tradeoffs matter when reducing small arrays repeatedly inside ODE right-hand-side and Jacobian-vector-product evaluations?

request.objective: Prioritize official LLVM vectorizer documentation and official Rust documentation. Extract the exact conditions under which floating-point reductions are vectorized, reassociation or fast-math requirements, stable std::arch CPU feature dispatch, and portable std::simd stability. Exclude forums, personal blogs and third-party summaries.
request.query: Official LLVM loop vectorizer documentation floating-point reductions ordered reductions reassociation flags and official Rust std::arch stable SIMD CPU runtime detection portable SIMD unstable documentation

request.objective: Prioritize original upstream GitHub repositories and authoritative crate documentation for Rust Rayon, pulp and wide. Find SIMD sqrt/div APIs, runtime architecture dispatch, versions and licenses, and explicit guarantees or warnings for floating-point parallel reductions. Exclude comparisons and unofficial summaries.
request.query: Official upstream Rust Rayon parallel iterator floating point reduction order documentation pulp runtime SIMD dispatch sqrt f64 wide f64x4 crate GitHub license

request.objective: Find original author papers, author-hosted PDFs or institutional repository full texts, and corresponding upstream code. Prioritize Collange/Defour/Graillat/Iakymchuk deterministic parallel summation, Demmel/Nguyen reproducible summation and Neumaier compensated summation. Extract the algorithmic conditions and limits for vectorization and reproducibility, not promotional speedup claims.
request.query: Original research paper full text deterministic bit accurate parallel floating point summation Collange Defour Graillat Iakymchuk ExBLAS ReproBLAS Demmel Nguyen compensated summation

request.searchQuestion: Which primary research papers explain when reusing right-hand-side evaluations, Jacobians, or Jacobian-vector-product data reduces the cost of implicit ordinary differential equation solvers without changing the solved equations, and how do they distinguish exact memoization at an identical state from approximate reuse across different states or steps?

sources.title: Rayon parallel iterator and bounded thread pools
reusable_principle_or_api: Independent work items can run via par_iter or bounded thread pool.
Upstream explicitly leaves sum/reduce combination order unspecified.
accuracy_reproducibility_limits: Floating-point par_iter().sum() is not a deterministic equivalent of the original sequential compensated sum.
Small inner tasks can be dominated by scheduling; nested pools can oversubscribe.
adoption_conditions: Prefer independent complete histories/banks or benchmark batches with stable outputIDs.
Keep each history solver/bank private; do not mix birth-state timelines.
Cap total active execution atactual8CPU/8GiB anduserlimits; do not mix parallel throughput with serial latency.
